children: shares fell 2.21% to $339.85 at 9:45 a.m. ET in regular trading on November 17, even after the retailer reported third-quarter results ahead of expectations and named CFO Richard McPhail its next chief executive. McPhail takes over on November 23, and Ted Decker moves to chairman. Ann-Marie Campbell becomes incoming president and chief operating officer.

Sales rose 4.9% to $43.4 billion, and comparable sales grew 2.2%. Adjusted EPS reached $3.86 versus $3.74 a year earlier, while GAAP EPS was $3.72. Adjusted operating margin slipped to 13.0% from 13.3%. For fiscal 2026, Home Depot now expects about 4.5% sales growth, about 1.4% comparable sales growth and adjusted EPS growth of about 2.0% from $14.69.

That guidance implies adjusted EPS of about $14.98 for the year, which puts the shares near 22.7 times earnings. That is a full multiple for a business growing earnings around 2%. GuruFocus gives Home Depot a GF Score of 84/100, with strong profitability offset by a middling balance sheet. Its GF Value of $388.05 implies a 12% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued, but closing that gap likely needs a housing recovery that has not arrived. The next test is McPhail's first fiscal 2027 outlook early next year.

title: Home Depot Stocks Fall 2.21% Despite Beat as CFO McPhail Named CEO
